Cracked
KRAKT
adjective (Gen-Z slang)
Gaming slang that spread through Fortnite and Twitch around 2018–2019: a player who is cracked is so skilled he seems almost unfair ("he’s cracked at building"). The exact source is uncertain; it likely draws on older cracked up (praised, as in "not all it’s cracked up to be") and on slang for someone wired and frantic. The irony a grandparent will catch: in their usage cracked meant broken, or slightly crazy ("he’s a bit cracked").

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

In current slang someone who is cracked is extremely skilled, especially at a video game, but also at a sport, an instrument, or a subject: "she’s cracked at chess." It is high praise for skill that looks almost unfair. The Christian observation: Scripture honours skill. God filled Bezaleel "with the spirit of God, in wisdom, and in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship" (Exo 31:3); the young David was recommended to a king as "cunning in playing" (1Sa 16:18); Benjamin sent warriors who "could use both the right hand and the left in hurling stones" (1Ch 12:2). "Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings" (Pro 22:29). Skill is a gift and a stewardship. The questions are where it is spent and whom it serves. A boy can be cracked at a game that will be forgotten in five years and unpractised at everything that will matter in fifty. And the Preacher gives the humbling footnote: "the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong... nor yet favour to men of skill; but time and chance happeneth to them all" (Ecc 9:11). A father tells his son: be cracked at something worth being good at, give God the credit for the hands He gave you, and remember that David’s skill with harp and sling served the LORD’s people, not a scoreboard.

Webster 1828 Definition

Gen-Z gaming slang (Fortnite and Twitch, c. 2018–2019) for extreme skill — a gift Scripture honours in Bezaleel and David, given to be spent where it matters and credited to its Giver.

CRACKED, adj. (Gen-Z slang, c. 2018–present; gaming origin) Extremely skilled; almost unfairly good. "Don’t queue against him, he’s cracked."

Cracked at a game, sport, or subject. Intensified: actually cracked, lowkey cracked.

Older senses a grandparent knows: split or broken ("a cracked cup"); slightly crazy ("he’s a bit cracked"); not all it’s cracked up to be.

Webster (1828), root word crack: “CRACK, verb transitive 1. To rend, break, or burst into chinks; to break partially; to divide the parts a little from each other; as, to crack a board or a rock; or to break without an entire severance of the parts; as, to crack glass, or ice. 2. To break in pieces; as, to crack nuts. 3. To break with grief; to affect deeply; to pain;”

Decode for parents: a compliment for skill. Ask what the skill is for.

Key Scripture

Exo 31:3 — "And I have filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, and in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship,"

1Sa 16:18 — "Then answered one of the servants, and said, Behold, I have seen a son of Jesse the Bethlehemite, that is cunning in playing, and a mighty valiant man, and a man of war, and prudent in matters, and a comely person, and the LORD is with him."

1Ch 12:2 — "They were armed with bows, and could use both the right hand and the left in hurling stones and shooting arrows out of a bow, even of Saul's brethren of Benjamin."

Pro 22:29 — "Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before mean men."

Ecc 9:11 — "I returned, and saw under the sun, that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favour to men of skill; but time and chance happeneth to them all."

Modern Corruption

Cracked praises real skill, which Scripture honours; the drift is spending a gift on what will not last, and taking the glory for hands God made.

expand to see more

Skill is a biblical good. The tabernacle was built by craftsmen the Spirit of God had filled (Exo 31:3), and the man diligent in his business stands before kings (Pro 22:29). There is nothing wrong with a boy who has put ten thousand hours into his reflexes. The question Scripture presses is stewardship: ten thousand hours is a decade of afternoons, and it can be spent on a game that will be patched out of existence or on a trade, an instrument, a language, a body trained for work.

The second danger is pride. A player who is cracked is easily worshipped by his lobby and easily convinced the skill is his own. Paul asks the question that ends that: "what hast thou that thou didst not receive?" (1Co 4:7). And the Preacher reminds us that "favour to men of skill" is not guaranteed; "time and chance happeneth to them all" (Ecc 9:11). Teach your children to get very good at worthwhile things, and to say thank you to the One who made their hands.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Old English cracian (to make a sharp noise, to break) → cracked, broken, then crazy → c. 2018–2019 Fortnite and Twitch: cracked, extremely skilled.

expand to see more

Old English cracian — to resound, to crack

Cracked — split, broken; later, mentally unsound

Cracked up — praised ("not all it’s cracked up to be")

c. 2018–2019: Fortnite and Twitch players called cracked

Now any extreme skill: cracked at chess, at math, at piano

Usage

""My little brother is cracked at Rocket League, it’s embarrassing.""

"God fills craftsmen with skill for His work (Exo 31:3)."
